Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for your time earlier — great conversation. Per our call, I summarized the open DPA/data-handling items below and next steps so your legal/security teams have a clear path forward. I attached a short PDF with the questions we captured (ACME_DPA_Questions.pdf).

Quick answers (details + documents to follow):
- Controller/Processor: Redwood acts as a processor for customer-provided input data (you are the controller). We process data only per customer instructions and our DPA reflects processor obligations.
- Subprocessors: We maintain a public subprocessor registry. We can provide the current list and point-in-time SOC 2 attestations.
- Breach notice: We commit to notify impacted customers and provide initial incident details within 72 hours of detection; follow-up with remediation timeline and root cause analysis as required by law and contract.
- Data residency: Hosted options in US and EU regions; for EU-only residency we can host data in our EU region or discuss Redwood Private deployment if you need stronger controls.
- Retention & logging: Default logs/audit trails retained 90 days; customer-configurable retention policies available (30/90/365 days options) and long-term exports on request.
- Encryption: Data encrypted in transit and at rest; we can share key management options (KMS/HSM) for Private deployments.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I’ll share a DPA clarifications doc and our security whitepaper.
2) Rachel (legal) and Dev (SE) can join a 1-hr legal+security sync to review any redlines and subprocessors.
3) If you want, we can provide a scoped SOC 2 report and an up-to-date subprocessor registry link.

Availability: I have time next Tue/Wed (Nov 3–4) afternoons PT — let me know what works for your team.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Sofia — attaching the DPA clarifications doc and our security whitepaper. Below are the written answers to your questions from the call.

1) Processor role
Redwood acts as a processor for customer-provided content (prompts, attachments, model inputs). We only process data under customer instructions; the DPA language in section 2.1 reflects our processor obligations and commitments to data minimization. (Excerpt included in attached DPA_Clarifications_v1.pdf.)

2) Subprocessors
We maintain a public subprocessor registry (link in the attached PDF). Current subprocessors include cloud infra providers and a managed logging vendor. Production data access is limited to (a) infra services that perform storage/compute, and (b) a managed logging provider for operational telemetry. We do not share raw customer prompts with analytics vendors. We can provide a point-in-time list and SOC 2 references on request.

3) Breach notice
We commit to an initial notification within 72 hours of detection with scope and impacted customer IDs where available; a follow-up remediation plan and RCA will be provided as soon as available. Rachel has included the recommended contractual language in the attached PDF.

4) Data residency & logs
Hosted options in the EU region are available for both model inputs and logs. For EU-only residency our Hosted EU option ensures data remains in EU regions; for stricter contractual guarantees we can discuss Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Logs can be configured to reside in EU only.

5) Encryption & SOC2
Data encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS. SOC 2 Type II report and additional compliance artifacts are available under NDA — I included the request link in the PDF.

Next steps:
- If ACME wants us to share the current subprocessors registry export and SOC 2 under NDA, we can do that immediately.
- Rachel is available for a legal sync. We propose Wed Nov 5 or Thu Nov 6 (11am–2pm ET).

If helpful, here are quick links: subprocessor registry (see attached DPA PDF), SOC 2 request: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cDPA-clarifications
